transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card services. My name is Marcus. May I have your full name, please?
Customer: Hi, yes, this is Tessa Brannigan.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Brannigan. For security, could you confirm your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure, the zip code is 44107 and the last four are 8821.
Agent: Thank you. You are verified. How can I help you today?
Customer: I was looking over my account and noticed a charge from Copper Kettle Bistro from September 21st that looks off. It's for $98.00.
Agent: I see that entry for $98.00 on September 21st. What occurred with this purchase?
Customer: Well, the food was $56.00, and I wrote down a $12 tip on the slip. But looking at the total, they took $98.00, so it seems like they put in a $42 tip instead.
Agent: Do you happen to have a copy of the receipt you signed or your customer copy?
Customer: Yes, I kept my copy from that night. It shows $56 for the meal, a $12 tip, and $68 at the bottom. Oh, and also, why did my annual fee go up recently? I noticed that on there too.
Agent: I can certainly look into the annual fee with you in just a moment, but first I want to make sure I have all the details noted for the restaurant charge. Have you reached out to Copper Kettle Bistro directly about the total?
Customer: I tried calling them twice last week, but the phone just rang and went to voicemail. Nobody ever called me back.
Agent: Did you leave a message with your phone number when you called?
Customer: Yes, I left my name, number, and the date I was there, but I never heard back from them.
Agent: Let me make sure I have the details captured correctly. You visited Copper Kettle Bistro on September 21st, your intended total was $68.00 with a $12 tip, but the final posted charge was $98.00 with a $42 tip, and you have your copy of the receipt showing that breakdown.
Customer: Yes, that is exactly what happened.
